title: Detection and census treat a page with no words as the lookup does, or say why they keep the soft-404 verdict
goal: factdiff.detect_source with lookup=False and census.py's check give a fetched page with no words (a client-rendered page: one newline) the same verdict the lookup gives (no soft-404, so no GONE in census and no gone in kbfacts' live word), or kb/_self/tools.md states why detection keeps it. Found by the SP-u5q37ds3 review (_tools/factdiff.py detect_source, _tools/census.py).

gates.question: Detection and census gave a page with no words the soft-404 verdict the lookup does not give: change detect_source to test the words of the text in both modes (two empty texts match any made-up page, so the verdict says nothing about the page), or keep detection's verdict and state why in tools.md?
options: detect_source tests words_key(text) in both modes, so census.py check reads no GONE for it
keep the soft-404 verdict in detection and state in tools.md why
gates.recommendation: detect_source tests words_key(text) in both modes, so census.py check reads no GONE for it
gates.answer: detect_source tests words_key(text) in both modes, so census.py check reads no GONE for it

notes: Premise: factdiff.detect_source on a fetched page whose text is one newline (made-up sibling answers the same) gave lookup=True verdict new and lookup=False verdict soft-404, so census.py:950 reports GONE (run 2026-10-13 at base, planted document and sibling; line 1138 reads words_key(text) only when lookup). Planned at the 2026-10-13 draft triage (sprint 4 of 15, "Freshness and census: the down window, the confirmable rule, soft 404s, unlocated anchors and mirror licences"): a lookup returns a wrong or missing fact until it is fixed, which the held-out answer-rate fitness test of EP-gzr4mmkm reads. The test named by the check drives census's check path (census.py:950) as well as detect_source, since the goal names both. Test ids are near the ceiling: extend the existing detect_source test and append the selector words to its name, a new id only when none does.
